gaps.sentence: English ___ (speak) as a first language in more than fifty countries.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive: is + spoken. Facts about the language, not about a speaker.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ (reach) by road until 1962; only mules could make the climb.
gaps.explanation: 'Until 1962' describes a past state of affairs: could not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: This machine ___ (NOT USE) for years before I repaired it.
gaps.hint: negative passive before a past point
gaps.explanation: The disuse continued up to the past repair: past perfect passive hadn't been used.

gaps.sentence: Your contract will ___ for a further twelve months.
gaps.explanation: After 'will', passive = be + past participle: will be renewed.

gaps.sentence: The stage was still wet — the scenery ___ (paint) only hours before.
gaps.explanation: 'Only hours before' points to the past perfect passive: had been + painted.

gaps.sentence: This form ___ (sign) in ink — digital signatures aren't valid.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle. Obligation: must (also has to) be signed.

gaps.sentence: My usual barber's chair ___ (fix), so I'm trying a new salon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: is being + fixed for an unfinished, ongoing repair.

gaps.sentence: The new policy ___ (CRITICISE) sharply since it was announced.
gaps.explanation: 'Since' + continuing result: present perfect passive has been criticised.
